title: Impact of Welfare Eligibility on Labor Supply

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the income eligibility cutoff (sharp if treatment equals the cutoff indicator; otherwise fuzzy RDD with the cutoff as an instrument).
- Why: Eligibility for welfare is determined by crossing an income threshold, providing quasi-random variation in treatment near the cutoff. The sample focuses on observations near the threshold, ideal for RDD.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: Potential outcomes (hours worked without treatment) vary smoothly with income at the cutoff.
  - No precise manipulation: Individuals cannot perfectly sort around the threshold.
  - For fuzzy RDD (if treatment imperfectly follows the cutoff): Relevance (jump in treatment probability at the cutoff) and monotonicity (no defiers).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load or install required packages
use_pkg <- function(p) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(p, character.only = TRUE))
}
use_pkg("sandwich")
use_pkg("lmtest")
use_pkg("AER")

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s92_data.csv"
dat <- read.csv(path)

# Inspect structure (optional)
# str(dat); head(dat)

# 2) Set cutoff (inferred from preview ~0.5)
c0 <- 0.5

# 3) Construct RD variables
dat$x <- dat$running_var
dat$y <- dat$y
dat$treat <- dat$treated  # eligibility indicator (observed)
dat$above <- as.integer(dat$x >= c0)  # cutoff indicator
dat$xc <- dat$x - c0

# 4) Check sharpness: how well does above match treat?
mismatch_rate <- mean(dat$treat != dat$above)
cat(sprintf("Sharpness check: share where treated != 1[x >= %.2f] = %.3f\n", c0, mismatch_rate))

# 5) Main estimation sample: observations flagged near the cutoff
if (!("near_cutoff" %in% names(dat))) {
  stop("near_cutoff column not found.")
}
main <- subset(dat, near_cutoff == 1)

# Helper function: robust summary printer
print_robust <- function(model, coef_name, label) {
  V <- sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC1")
  ct <- lmtest::coeftest(model, vcov = V)
  if (!(coef_name %in% rownames(ct))) {
    stop(paste("Coefficient", coef_name, "not found in model. Available:", paste(rownames(ct), collapse=", ")))
  }
  est <- ct[coef_name, "Estimate"]
  se  <- ct[coef_name, "Std. Error"]
  t   <- ct[coef_name, "t value"]
  p   <- ct[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  cat(sprintf("%s: estimate = %.4f, SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.3f\n", label, est, se, t, p))
  invisible(list(est=est, se=se, t=t, p=p))
}

# 6) Reduced-form RD (jump in y at cutoff)
rf_mod <- lm(y ~ above + xc + above:xc, data = main)
rf <- print_robust(rf_mod, "above", "Reduced-form jump in hours at cutoff (RF)")

# 7) First stage (jump in treatment at cutoff)
fs_mod <- lm(treat ~ above + xc + above:xc, data = main)
fs <- print_robust(fs_mod, "above", "First-stage jump in eligibility at cutoff (FS)")

# 8) Fuzzy RD (2SLS): LATE of eligibility on hours at cutoff
iv_mod <- AER::ivreg(y ~ treat + xc + above:xc | above + xc + above:xc, data = main)
# Robust (HC1) inference
iv_vcov <- sandwich::vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- lmtest::coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = iv_vcov)
if (!("treat" %in% rownames(iv_ct))) stop("IV model did not include 'treat' coefficient.")
iv_est <- iv_ct["treat", "Estimate"]
iv_se  <- iv_ct["treat", "Std. Error"]
iv_t   <- iv_ct["treat", "t value"]
iv_p   <- iv_ct["treat", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Main Fuzzy RD (2SLS) LATE of eligibility on hours: %.4f (SE=%.4f), t=%.2f, p=%.3f\n",
            iv_est, iv_se, iv_t, iv_p))

# Also report weak-instrument diagnostic (non-robust F for convenience)
iv_diag <- summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)
fs_F <- iv_diag$diagnostics["Weak instruments", "statistic"]
cat(sprintf("First-stage weak-instrument F-stat (non-robust): %.2f\n", fs_F))

# 9) Sharp RD (if very sharp assignment): treat cutoff indicator as treatment
sharp_mod <- lm(y ~ above + xc + above:xc, data = main)
sharp <- print_robust(sharp_mod, "above", "Sharp RD estimate (if assignment is sharp)")

# 10) Bandwidth robustness with triangular kernel and IV
bandwidths <- c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20)
bw_results <- data.frame(bw = bandwidths, iv_est = NA, iv_se = NA, iv_p = NA, n = NA)
for (i in seq_along(bandwidths)) {
  h <- bandwidths[i]
  win <- subset(dat, abs(xc) <= h)
  if (nrow(win) < 30) next
  w <- 1 - abs(win$xc)/h  # triangular kernel weights in window
  # 2SLS with weights
  iv_bw <- try(AER::ivreg(y ~ treat + xc + above:xc | above + xc + above:xc, data = win, weights = w), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(iv_bw, "try-error")) next
  Vbw <- sandwich::vcovHC(iv_bw, type = "HC1")
  ctbw <- lmtest::coeftest(iv_bw, vcov = Vbw)
  if (!("treat" %in% rownames(ctbw))) next
  bw_results$iv_est[i] <- ctbw["treat", "Estimate"]
  bw_results$iv_se[i]  <- ctbw["treat", "Std. Error"]
  bw_results$iv_p[i]   <- ctbw["treat", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  bw_results$n[i]      <- nrow(win)
}
cat("Bandwidth robustness (fuzzy RD with triangular kernel):\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(bw_results))) {
  if (is.na(bw_results$iv_est[i])) next
  cat(sprintf("  h=%.2f: LATE=%.4f (SE=%.4f), p=%.3f, N=%d\n",
              bw_results$bw[i], bw_results$iv_est[i], bw_results$iv_se[i],
              bw_results$iv_p[i], bw_results$n[i]))
}

# 11) Optional: Global quadratic RD (parametric robustness, sharp specification)
quad_mod <- lm(y ~ above + poly(xc, 2, raw = TRUE) + above:poly(xc, 2, raw = TRUE), data = dat)
quad <- print_robust(quad_mod, "above", "Global quadratic RD (sharp, parametric)")

# 12) Final printed summary
cat("\nSummary:\n")
cat(sprintf("- Main 2SLS LATE (eligibility on hours): %.4f (SE=%.4f), p=%.3f\n", iv_est, iv_se, iv_p))
cat(sprintf("- Reduced-form jump (hours at cutoff): %.4f (SE=%.4f), p=%.3f\n", rf$est, rf$se, rf$p))
cat(sprintf("- First-stage jump (eligibility at cutoff): %.4f (SE=%.4f), p=%.3f; Weak-IV F=%.2f\n", fs$est, fs$se, fs$p, fs_F))
cat(sprintf("- Sharp RD (if assignment is sharp): %.4f (SE=%.4f), p=%.3f\n", sharp$est, sharp$se, sharp$p))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Eligibility for welfare is expected to reduce hours worked through income effects and high implicit marginal tax rates near the threshold.
- Magnitude: Modest. For standardized hours, a decline around 0.05 to 0.15 SD is plausible; if hours are in weekly units, roughly 1–3 fewer hours per week near the cutoff. The exact estimate will be the local average treatment effect at the threshold.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Examine changes in labor supply around the income threshold for welfare eligibility.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Crossing the income threshold for welfare eligibility results in a reduction in labor supply.
